newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says about 200 tax payments misdirected.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says about 200 tax payments misdirected.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry said Sunday that its fraud investigators uncovered about 200 cases in which tax payments to the Federal Treasury have been misdirected and diverted into private hands.
"Through altering checks, payments were not deposited in the Treasury but were diverted to business accounts or private accounts that, in many cases, were fictious," the ministry said in a statement.
Of the cases uncovered, it said the total amount of taxes not in government coffers as a result was 428 million pesos.
"As it can be appreciated from the number of cases, it is not a question of a widespread problem," the ministry said.
It said the Finance Ministry receives about seven million returns per year. It did not say over what period or when the 200 cases were uncovered.

It added that although it could be supposed some of the fraud could have been done with the collusion of bank employees, it is also investigating the possibility that employees of the ministry could have been involved in the operations.
To date, no such evidence has been found, it added.
Mexico Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz reiterated on Friday the government is investigating bank officials on charges of hoarding public tax money.

"There have been some instances in which taxpayers, mostly companies, have made tax payments through banks and unfortunately there have been some banking officials ... that divert the tax payments for other purposes," he said.
The Finance Ministry recently launched an extensive campaign to persuade Mexicans to pay their taxes, arresting wealthy tax evaders and warning: "Pay Your Taxes, Don't Pay the Consequences."
